findings.title: Mid-run hold ends when a UI-launched program's adapter call returns
findings.scenario: Workstation approves an EXECUTE, non-Calculator UI action (computer.invoke_control, or a trusted-desktop UI run) whose effect launches a program that reads project files later. bus.request adds the run to liveCode (line 308) and removes it in the finally block (line 349) as soon as the adapter returns, which is before the launched program finishes. A paired-device filesystem.write admitted during that program's lifetime is not held, because remoteMutationHeld (manager.server.ts:2380-2392) and liveCodeExecutions (manager.server.ts:2361-2377) see no live code. The device write is recorded as a pending change only after it lands, so the program reads device-approved content that the workstation never reviewed. The same window exists for trusted-desktop UI runs: desktopExecutions liveness (manager.server.ts:186) follows the run row status, which also finishes when the adapter returns.
findings.evidence: Probe (scratch folder, deleted afterwards; no repo writes, no tests run). A custom EXECUTE adapter 'computer.invoke_control' spawned a detached child that wrote a marker 2.5 s later. Inside execute(): liveCodeExecutions() = ['computer.invoke_control']; remoteMutationHeld(device-remote-envelope filesystem.write) = 'Approval required on Windows Host: code approved on the Windows Host is running ...'. After bus.request resolved (decision allow / succeeded): liveCodeExecutions() = [], remoteMutationHeld(...) = null, child still alive, and the launched program wrote its marker afterwards. Adapter return time is the only end point for liveCode; no owned-process tracking covers UI-launched children. Note: terminal.exec and git runs are not affected on Windows because owned groups use KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE (native/bunny-owned-process.c:85).
findings.recommendation: Keep UI-automation EXECUTE runs (computer.invoke_control, computer.type with side effects, computer.open_app of non-Calculator targets) live for a bounded window after the adapter returns, or track the launched process tree from the UI action. Alternatively hold device-attributed mutations for a fixed interval after any non-Calculator EXECUTE run. Add a regression test that drives a UI-launch adapter and asserts a device write stays held until the launched process ends or the window closes.

findings.title: Device-attributed writes inside skill steps cannot be unblocked by a workstation answer while code is live
findings.scenario: remoteMutationHeld exempts a held write only when step.executor.kind === 'capability' and the workstation one-time answer names the same action. For a skill step the exemption never applies, so a device-attributed write in that step is held for as long as any code is live. Each workstation allow_once re-runs the step, which is held again and produces a new desktop-required ask. The loop ends only when the live code ends or the workstation stops the Mission.
findings.evidence: Code read only, not probed. Reachable when a device-driven Mission has a skill step whose envelope lacks EXECUTE (deviceStartRefusal, manager.server.ts ~2200, permits this) and a workstation code run is live. The exemption line is 'if (step.executor.kind === "capability" && once?.action === request.action && isTrustedLocalActor(...)) return null;'.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same one-time exemption to skill steps when the answered request's action and desktopOperation match the held request, or report the hold once with the live-code reason so the workstation is not asked repeatedly for the same write.

findings.title: Device revocation scans only the 500 most recent Missions for unexecuted one-time answers
findings.scenario: endDeviceAnswers iterates this.store.missions(500). That query is ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 500 (store.server.ts:105), so a non-terminal step in an older Mission keeps a revoked device's approvedOnce. When the workstation later resumes that Mission, the stale one-time allowance is applied under the revoked device's answer, which conflicts with the policy that revocation ends unexecuted one-time answers.
findings.evidence: Code read only, not probed. Reproduction needs a device one-time answer that is still unexecuted (for example a verification-phase allowance on a step that re-asks, or a step paused after the answer), more than 500 newer Missions, then revocation and a workstation resume. The fix is to iterate the non-terminal Missions (missionsIn with the active states) instead of the newest 500.
findings.recommendation: Iterate every non-terminal Mission (store.missionsIn with the non-terminal state list) in endDeviceAnswers, not the newest 500 Missions, and add a test with more than 500 Missions.

- manager.server.ts:2361-2377 (liveCodeExecutions) reads only bus.liveCode, provider sessions, and tasks.lingering. Capability-run children are never added to lingering (lingering.set happens only in bunny-host/manager.server.ts:1711-1736, for provider tasks). The computer adapter never pushes to processOwnership, so Start-Process or UI-launched children are untracked.

Concrete reachability, stronger than the finding's example: computer.server.ts:13 allowlists APPS including "terminal": "wt.exe". computer.server.ts:374-377 starts it with Start-Process, and the process outlives the adapter. For a workstation-approved open_app of terminal, the launched shell is a live code-running environment that Bunny starts. Remote non-Calculator open_app is not device-approvable (remoteExecutionRefusal). Yet after the approved call returns, a paired-device filesystem.write of a data/document type in that folder is admitted with no hold, and the Host-wide review gate only blocks new Bunny-started runs, not the already-running shell. The round-4 design comment at manager.server.ts:2222 and the hold's stated purpose ("while workstation-approved code is live") cover this case, so the gap breaks the intended invariant.

Why not refuted: the accepted-limitation carve-out covers programs Bunny "never runs or never observed" and tools "the owner starts outside Bunny". The terminal and UI-launched programs here are started by Bunny's own approved capability, so the carve-out does not clearly apply. The device cannot itself execute code, and writes are limited to data/document types, so the realistic impact needs a workstation-approved program or the user to act on device-written content. That keeps this at MEDIUM rather than HIGH or BLOCKER.

Minor correction to the finding: the cited line numbers are accurate (bus 308 and 349; manager 2361-2377 and 2380-2392). The recommendation is sound.

findings.title: Held paired-device write loses its attribution when the workstation answers the hold, so it never reaches the review gate
findings.scenario: Workstation-approved Mission M2 (not started by a device, no remote envelope) has a filesystem.write step that asks each time. While workstation code (terminal.exec in Mission M1) is live, the paired device answers allow_once on M2's write ask. remoteMutationHeld (bus.server.ts:165) holds the write and raises a new desktopRequired ask. The workstation answers that ask allow_once. respond() (manager.server.ts:3806) overwrites step.approvedOnce with the workstation request, so remoteActorFor() (manager.server.ts:2321) no longer finds a device answer. The write then runs and remoteMutationStarted (bus.server.ts:307) is skipped, so no remote_changes row is recorded. The Host-wide review gate never sees the change, and the next workstation-approved terminal.exec runs over device-written content with no review prompt. The workstation's prompt for the held write shows only 'code ... is running' and no path or content. Control run (no workstation code live when the device answers): the write is recorded (pendingRemoteChanges=1) and the next terminal.exec is blocked with a desktopRequired review ask.
findings.evidence: Probe (throwaway, mkdtemp under OS temp, removed afterwards; repo modules imported by absolute file URL). Setup: capability.grant ask_every_time on filesystem.write (global); workstation approve of write mission; workstation terminal run slow.mjs in flight (liveCode.size==1); device mission.respond allow_once on the write ask. The code path is in the diff: manager.server.ts:2310-2325 (remoteActorFor), :2384-2386 (remoteMutationHeld workstation one-time exemption), :3806 (approvedOnce overwrite on execute path), bus.server.ts:165 and :307.
findings.recommendation: Keep paired-device origin across the hold: record the remote change (store.recordRemoteChange) when the held ask is created, or persist the device origin on the step/request (for example a field set when a device answer or held device change is created) that a later workstation approvedOnce cannot erase. Show the held path and the change listing (remoteChanges) in the held prompt, and add a test variant of F01-R27 on a workstation-envelope, non-device-started Mission asserting pendingRemoteChanges after the workstation allow and a review ask on the next code run.

findings.title: Device revocation misses one-time answers on Missions older than the 500 newest
findings.scenario: endDeviceAnswers(actor) is meant to end a revoked device's unexecuted one-time answers (T9R-F01 (D)). Not refuted. The core claim holds and was probed. verification.server.ts:56-61 runs `python <path>` via execOwnedFile with no remote-envelope check, no pendingRemoteReview gate and no desktop grant. The probe in a temp folder (cleaned up, no repo tests run) called validateVerifySpec + verifySpec on a hello.py containing print("BUNNY_X"): spec accepted, inertDataPath false, verifySpec returned passed:true and actually ran python. The call site (bunny-host/manager.server.ts:1441-1458) has no review or envelope check. The review gate is enforced only in the bus (manager.server.ts:177/178, 1451, 124) and in provider launch, not for this path, and the gate's listed categories do not include verification.

The finding understates reachability. Its claim that devices cannot create the .py file holds only for direct one-time answers (remoteExecutionRefusal/inertDataPath at authorization.server.ts:233, used at manager.server.ts:2109). It does not hold for a device-started Mission: mission.start and mission.approve are REMOTE-allowed (commands.server.ts:27). deviceStartRefusal (manager.server.ts:2184-2201) refuses only runsCode operations and shell-capable sessions, and filesystem.write is not runsCode. deviceMissionRefusal (2115-2127) checks only manifest risk. For a workstation-envelope Mission, the bus applies remoteExecutionRefusal only when isRemoteEnvelope (authorization.server.ts:364-367), so a workstation-authored plan step filesystem.write of hello.py is not inert-checked. That step, plus an agent step carrying task_spec python verification, lets the device trigger the Python run. The child must be tool-free (for example local Ollama) so it is not held by the review gate, which the probe did not exercise end to end.

Impact is still low. The executed program is constrained to a single print of a validated plain-text string, the file must match exactly, and the content is workstation-authored plan content. So this is a policy deviation (Python run authorized through a device-approved plan, outside the Host-wide review gate and remote ceiling), not arbitrary code execution. LOW is the right severity; the recommendation (refuse python verification under remote-attributed or device-driven Missions, or gate it with the review check) stands.
